description: M4 reconciliation worker: five SQL checks in ONE REPEATABLE READ transaction (job_locks FOR UPDATE NOWAIT FIRST), one reconciliation_runs row + one reconciliation_problems row per problem, never fixes; node-cron schedule in worker.ts + POST /admin/reconciliation/run (409 RECON_LOCKED when locked); optional 24h idempotency-key cleanup. Depends on FEAT-004 (full money path + routes). Independent of FEAT-006 but ordered before it so the admin router exists.
steps: Create src/services/reconciliationService.ts: run() opens withTransaction at REPEATABLE READ and executes, as the FIRST statement, SELECT ... FROM job_locks WHERE job_name='reconciliation' FOR UPDATE NOWAIT; on 55P03/lock-not-available catch -> early exit signalling locked (maps to 409 RECON_LOCKED for the manual trigger) having done no scan work. Then run the five checks each as a single query per design §13: (a) global SUM(debit)=SUM(credit) over ledger_entries; (b) per-transfer GROUP BY transfer_id HAVING SUM(debit)<>SUM(credit); (c) per-account stored accounts.balance vs computed SUM(credit)-SUM(debit); (d) computed balance<0 on any non-system account; (e) orphan entries (transfer_id/account_id pointing nowhere) AND settled transfers with no entries using the EXACT predicate status IN ('COMPLETED','REVERSED') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM ledger_entries le WHERE le.transfer_id=t.id). Write one reconciliation_runs row (started_at, finished_at, status ok|problems|error, global_ok, problem_count, per-check counts) and one reconciliation_problems row per problem (check_name, entity_id, expected, actual). The job REPORTS, never fixes.

Add job error handling: a check query that errors marks the run status='error', records the failing check, rolls back, releases the lock (txn end), logs at error. Lock-held is an expected non-error early exit logged at info.
Add optional, config-gated (IDEMPOTENCY_CLEANUP_HOURS) deletion of idempotency_keys older than 24h in the same run.

Create src/http/routes/admin.ts with POST /admin/reconciliation/run (triggers reconciliationService.run; returns 202 {run_id} or 409 RECON_LOCKED) and a stub for POST /admin/transfers/{id}/release implemented in FEAT-006 (or implement release here if FEAT-006 ordering makes it cleaner — but the release money logic belongs with fraud/hold in FEAT-006; wire the route and return 409 TRANSFER_NOT_HELD until FEAT-006 fills in the HELD completion). Mount the admin router in app.ts. These POSTs are idempotency-exempt per design §8.

Create src/worker.ts: build pool from env, run migrations if needed, schedule the nightly reconciliation via node-cron (RECON_CRON), and allow the admin-trigger path to invoke the same run (the DB lock guarantees single-run regardless of source).

Create test/integration/reconciliation.test.ts covering AC-6 (seed 10,000 settled COMPLETED transfers with balanced entries; corrupt exactly three things via direct SQL -- alter one entry's amount, delete one credit entry, alter one stored balance; run the job; assert exactly 3 reconciliation_problems with the correct check_name/expected/actual and nothing else, plus one reconciliation_runs row) and AC-7 (hold the job_locks row in one txn, trigger run, assert immediate exit and POST /admin/reconciliation/run returns 409 RECON_LOCKED).
acceptance_criteria: Against a real Postgres: AC-6 reports EXACTLY the three injected problems and nothing else (settled-only orphan predicate prevents a false fourth from any HELD/FAILED rows), with one run row and three problem rows; AC-7 second concurrent invocation exits immediately / returns 409 RECON_LOCKED.
The job never mutates ledger/accounts to 'fix' anything; it only writes run + problem rows.
job_locks FOR UPDATE NOWAIT is the first statement in the recon transaction.
verification: If Postgres reachable: npm run migrate then npx vitest run test/integration/reconciliation.test.ts -> pass (reconciliation is a STEP-4 acceptance test).
If no Postgres in-environment: record in findings that recon integration tests were authored but NOT executed (no Postgres); keep tsc clean. Do NOT fabricate a pass.
findings:
COMPLETED (code + tests authored and typecheck-verified; Postgres-dependent reconciliation integration tests AUTHORED but NOT executed — no Postgres/Docker in this environment).

VERIFICATION RUN LOCALLY (Node v26.8.1, via `node node_modules/...` because PowerShell execution policy blocks npm.ps1/npx.ps1 shims; output captured to temp files then deleted):
- `node node_modules/typescript/bin/tsc --noEmit` -> EXIT 0, zero errors (all new/changed src + the new reconciliation.test.ts compile under strict + noUncheckedIndexedAccess + exactOptionalPropertyTypes).
- `node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run` -> EXIT 0: 15 unit tests pass; all integration suites SKIP automatically (describe.skipIf(SKIP_INTEGRATION) because DATABASE_URL is unset). The new reconciliation.test.ts is COLLECTED (2 tests: AC-6, AC-7) and skips cleanly — confirming it compiles and is discoverable, but it was NEVER executed against a real Postgres. No reconciliation pass against Postgres is claimed.

HONESTY NOTE (no Postgres here): Docker and psql are NOT on PATH. AC-6 and AC-7 require a migrated real Postgres and were NOT run. With a real DATABASE_URL + migrated DB (CI postgres:15 service or local Postgres) they will run.

WHAT WAS IMPLEMENTED (design §13, §16, FR-10):
1. src/services/reconciliationService.ts — `run(pool, options?, logger?)`:
   - Opens withTransaction at REPEATABLE READ. The FIRST statement is `SELECT job_name FROM job_locks WHERE job_name='reconciliation' FOR UPDATE NOWAIT` (acquireJobLock). On SQLSTATE 55P03 (lock-not-available) it throws an internal ReconLockHeld sentinel caught by run() -> returns `{ kind:'locked' }` having done NO scan work (design §13 'lock first', fail-fast). Then UPDATEs job_locks.locked_at/locked_by for observability.
   - The five checks, each a single SQL query (design §13): (a) global_balance — SUM(amount) FILTER debit vs credit over all ledger_entries (one aggregate row; entity_id NULL); (b) per_transfer_balance — GROUP BY transfer_id HAVING SUM(debit)<>SUM(credit); (c) stored_vs_computed — accounts.balance vs COALESCE(SUM(credit)-SUM(debit),0) via LEFT JOIN (covers zero-entry accounts; system accounts included, baseline 0==0 per finding 2a); (d) negative_balance — non-system accounts whose COMPUTED balance < 0; (e) orphan — ledger_entries whose transfer_id/account_id point nowhere UNION settled transfers with no entries using the EXACT predicate `status IN ('COMPLETED','REVERSED') AND NOT EXISTS(SELECT 1 FROM ledger_entries le WHERE le.transfer_id=t.id)`. The settled-only filter means HELD/FAILED/PENDING transfers (which legitimately have zero entries) are NEVER reported.
   - Writes ONE reconciliation_runs row (started_at, finished_at, status ok|problems, global_ok, problem_count, and the five per-check count columns) + ONE reconciliation_problems row per problem (check_name, entity_id, expected, actual). The job REPORTS, never fixes — it issues NO UPDATE/DELETE against ledger_entries or accounts.
   - Error handling (design §13): a check/write query that errors rolls back the txn (releasing the lock), then records a status='error' reconciliation_runs row on a FRESH pool connection (best-effort audit) and returns `{ kind:'error', message }`; logged at error. Lock-held is an expected non-error early exit logged at info.
   - Optional cleanup: when options.idempotencyCleanupHours > 0, DELETE idempotency_keys older than that many hours in the SAME transaction (design §13). The worker passes IDEMPOTENCY_CLEANUP_HOURS on the scheduled run only; the admin trigger runs checks only (no cleanup).
   - Exported types for FEAT-006/convergence: ReconciliationOutcome = {kind:'completed';runId;status;problemCount} | {kind:'locked'} | {kind:'error';message}, CheckName, Problem, RunOptions, ReconLogger.
2. src/http/routes/admin.ts — `adminRouter(pool)` with TWO routes, BOTH idempotency-exempt (NOT wired to requireIdempotency; design §8 'Idempotency scope'):
   - POST /admin/reconciliation/run -> calls reconciliationService.run({ lockedBy:'admin-trigger' }); `locked` -> throws AppError('RECON_LOCKED') => 409; `error` -> AppError('INTERNAL') => 500; `completed` -> 202 { run_id, status, problem_count, request_id }.
   - POST /admin/transfers/:id/release -> STUB for FEAT-006: validates the id param then throws AppError('TRANSFER_NOT_HELD') => 409. FEAT-006 fills in the HELD-completion money logic (re-lock, re-check funds, write ledger entries, audit HELD->COMPLETED/HELD->FAILED per design §9.1.1).
3. src/http/app.ts — mounted `adminRouter(pool)` after statementRouter and BEFORE errorMiddleware (same pattern as the other routers).
4. src/worker.ts (NEW) — worker entrypoint (design §5/§16): loadConfig, createPool, runMigrations if needed, validate RECON_CRON via cron.validate, then cron.schedule(RECON_CRON, ...) a nightly reconciliation. The scheduled tick calls the SAME reconciliationService.run with { lockedBy:'cron', idempotencyCleanupHours: config.IDEMPOTENCY_CLEANUP_HOURS }; errors are caught/logged (never thrown out of the cron callback) so a failed run does not crash the worker and cron retries next schedule. The job_locks NOWAIT lock guarantees single-run regardless of trigger source (cron vs admin). (node-cron + @types/node-cron are already deps; package.json already has start:worker -> node dist/src/worker.js.)
5. test/integration/reconciliation.test.ts (NEW) — through the REAL HTTP app (listen(0) + fetch) and the service directly, guarded by describe.skipIf(SKIP_INTEGRATION):
   - AC-6: seeds 10,000 COMPLETED peer transfers (ring of 50 wallets, batched multi-row INSERTs in one txn) with balanced debit/credit entries and stored balances set to the exact computed net so the BASELINE run is clean (asserted: 0 problems). Then injects corruptions and asserts EXACTLY 3 reconciliation_problems across EXACTLY three check_names + one reconciliation_runs row with matching per-check counts.
   - AC-7: opens a holder txn that SELECTs the reconciliation job_locks row FOR UPDATE, then asserts (i) a direct service run() returns { kind:'locked' } (immediate exit, no scan) and (ii) POST /admin/reconciliation/run returns 409 with body.code === 'RECON_LOCKED'; releases the holder in finally.

AC-6 PROBLEM-COUNT MODEL (IMPORTANT — read before changing the seed/corruptions): the five checks are NOT mutually independent. The global sum IS the sum of the per-transfer sums, so it is mathematically IMPOSSIBLE to unbalance exactly one transfer (per_transfer_balance) without also unbalancing the global total (global_balance), or vice versa — any single-transfer imbalance of +delta makes BOTH checks fire. The task step-6 phrasing lists three raw corruptions ('alter one entry's amount, delete one credit entry, alter one stored balance'), but 'alter one entry's amount' ALONE fires THREE checks (global + per-transfer + stored-vs-computed on the touched account) unless side effects are compensated. To land EXACTLY 3 problem rows the test injects TWO carefully-compensated corruptions that together drive EXACTLY three DISTINCT checks and nothing else:
   (1) add ONE extra `debit` ledger_entry to a settled transfer tA (INSERT is allowed; the insert-only trigger blocks only UPDATE/DELETE) -> fires global_balance AND per_transfer_balance(tA); then lower tA's source account STORED balance by the same delta so stored_vs_computed does NOT fire for it.
   (2) bump a SPARE zero-entry account's STORED balance by +1 -> fires stored_vs_computed only (1>=0 so negative_balance stays quiet).
   Net = exactly 3 rows: global_balance (entity_id NULL), per_transfer_balance (entity_id=tA, expected=credit sum, actual=debit sum), stored_vs_computed (entity_id=spare, expected=1, actual=0); orphan_count=0, negative_balance_count=0. This is the deterministic, Postgres-truthful realization of AC-6's intent ('exactly those problems and nothing else'); it was NOT run against Postgres (none here). A convergence/fixer step with a real DB should confirm the exact-3 count and, if desired, add a third isolated corruption only via a check that CAN be isolated (e.g. a settled-no-entries orphan with compensated stored balances, or a negative_balance that also tolerates the paired stored drift).

ADMIN ROUTER SHAPE (for FEAT-006's release endpoint): the router is `adminRouter(pool: Pool): Router` exported from src/http/routes/admin.ts and mounted in src/http/app.ts before errorMiddleware. FEAT-006 should EXTEND this same router: replace the body of the existing `router.post('/admin/transfers/:id/release', ...)` STUB (which currently validates the id via parseOrThrow(idParamSchema, req.params) and throws AppError('TRANSFER_NOT_HELD')) with the real single-transaction release. Both admin POSTs stay idempotency-exempt (do NOT add requireIdempotency). The release success shape per design §8 is 200 { transfer_id, status, request_id }; a non-HELD transfer -> 409 TRANSFER_NOT_HELD; a HELD transfer whose sender is now short on release -> HELD->FAILED, 422 INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS (design §9.1.1/§17). The transferService fraud seam `evaluateFraud` (src/services/transferService.ts) is still a no-op returning { decision:'proceed' } and the HELD commit-with-no-entries branch is structurally present but unexercised — FEAT-006 owns both the hold decision and the release completion.
